metadata.title: MCP Integration.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether connecting a Claude Code plugin to an external service is a thing you ask for or a thing you configure, using the mcp-integration skill's own Asana tool-naming convention as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that MCP integration is a config entry with an exact connection type and tool name, and either one wrong fails silently.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the exact Asana tool name, mcp__plugin_asana_asana__asana_create_task: exact match fires precisely, one underscore off fires silently, a wildcard also fires but widens scope)

beats.narration_text: Someone asks how to add an app to their plugin so it can use Asana. But there's no app step — you configure an MCP server, choosing one of four connection types. What's in that config?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I add an app to my Claude plugin so it can use Asana?', hesitates on 'app', corrects to 'MCP server', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I add an app
to my Claude plugin

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('app' -> 'MCP server') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: To reach an external service, a plugin declares it — in a config file, as one of four connection types. If this were like installing an app, one setting would work for everything. It doesn't: a local script Claude spawns itself needs stdio; a hosted service authenticating with OAuth, like Asana, needs SSE instead. Pick the wrong type, and Claude can't reach it.

shot.new_visual_element: One config box branching to four labelled connection types; a mismatched type crossed out, unreachable

production_viz.label: One declaration, four types
production_viz.mechanic: A single config box at top labelled 'external service' branches down into four cards: stdio, SSE, HTTP, WebSocket. A fifth ghost card reading 'one app-install setting' fades in center, gets a terracotta strike through it, and dissolves. Then a local-script icon connects cleanly to the stdio card; a hosted-OAuth icon (Asana) tries to connect to stdio instead, and the line breaks with a small terracotta X before rerouting to SSE, which connects cleanly.

beats.narration_text: Two places to write that declaration. A dedicated dot-mcp-dot-json file at the plugin's root — the usual choice with more than one server. Or an inline mcpServers field inside plugin-dot-json, for a single simple server. Say the Asana server goes in dot-mcp-dot-json, type SSE. Each tool it offers gets a fixed name: mcp, two underscores, plugin, underscore, the plugin name, underscore, the server name, two underscores, the tool name. Asana's create-task tool becomes mcp__plugin_asana_asana__asana_create_task — exactly that string, with two underscores between each section.

shot.new_visual_element: Two config file shapes; THE ANCHOR — the exact tool-name string built piece by piece

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one exact string
production_viz.mechanic: Two file cards fade in side by side: '.mcp.json' (recommended, multiple servers) and 'plugin.json / mcpServers' (single server). Both fade out. THE ANCHOR. The tool-name string builds left to right in monospace, segment by segment, each segment briefly highlighted as it's named: mcp__ / plugin_ / asana_ / asana__ / asana_create_task, assembling into the full string mcp__plugin_asana_asana__asana_create_task, which then holds, centered, large. THIS EXACT STRING RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Get that name exactly right, and Claude calls exactly that one tool — nothing more, nothing less. Get one underscore wrong, and nothing happens: no error, just silence, because a name mismatch isn't reported. Some plugins pre-allow with a wildcard instead, to dodge that risk — asana star matches every tool the server offers, not just create-task. That also fires without error. But now the plugin can call anything Asana exposes, which is exactly what the specific name was there to prevent.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the exact string firing cleanly on one tool; then a wildcard string lighting up every tool on the same server

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — exact vs wildcard
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 STRING RETURNS, identical, and fires cleanly into a single lit tool card: 'asana_create_task'. Then one character is swapped (the final underscore run breaks), the string dims, and 'no error. no strike. just silence.' appears beside it in serif italic. Below, a wildcard string 'mcp__plugin_asana_asana__*' appears and lights up every tool card the Asana server offers, all at once, in teal — no error there either, but now the whole row is lit instead of one card.

beats.narration_text: Adding an MCP server isn't an app install — it's a config entry with the right connection type and an exact tool name. Get either wrong, and it fails quietly, not loudly.

props.quote: Adding an MCP server isn't an app install — it's a config entry with the right connection type and an exact tool name. Get either wrong, and it fails quietly, not loudly.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Add an MCP server to my plugin that connects to Asana for task management. Watch three things when Claude answers: does the configuration land in dot-mcp-dot-json, not inline inside plugin-dot-json? Is the type set to SSE — not stdio, not HTTP — since Asana is a hosted service using OAuth? And does the command's allowed-tools list the exact tool name, mcp__plugin_asana_asana__asana_create_task, rather than a wildcard? Liam, in for Bear.
